summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, pseudotumor cerebri with a VP shunt, obstructive sleep apnea, depression, and obesity was admitted for substernal chest pain radiating to the back and jaw. Initial evaluation showed no acute coronary syndrome, with normal troponins and EKG. A cardiac catheterization revealed a patent stent in the right coronary artery and no high-grade stenosis, though elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure was noted without clinical heart failure. The chest pain was ultimately attributed to a likely esophageal etiology, such as GERD, and managed with pantoprazole and TUMS. GI follow-up was arranged for outpatient endoscopy. She also developed mild right forearm swelling post-cath, which resolved with conservative treatment and was confirmed as non-thrombotic on ultrasound. She remained stable, adherent to medications, and was discharged home with plans for cardiology and GI follow-up.
problems: Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
Presence of cerebrospinal fluid drainage device
